editorial:
You follow a charming waiter who dreams of becoming a big-shot entrepreneur, so he starts pretending to be an important businessman. The setup is easy to enjoy because the lies snowball fast, and every fancy dinner or business meeting becomes a new chance for things to go wrong. The main character is likable, the upper-class world feels flashy, and the comedy comes from watching him bluff his way through situations he barely understands. It has a light, upbeat vibe that keeps you smiling even when the plan starts falling apart.

The acting sells the chaos, especially when the waiter has to switch between humble service and fake confidence. The pacing moves quickly, with plenty of awkward moments and funny misunderstandings. Some jokes are predictable, and a few side characters feel thin, but the heart keeps it fun.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the waiter's fake identity is exposed during a major business event, and the people he impressed turn against him. Instead of giving up, he uses the skills he learned while pretending to pitch a real, honest business idea. The twist is that his charm and work ethic were genuine all along, so he earns a second chance without the lie. He leaves the fake businessman life behind and starts building success for real.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves light comedies about big dreams and funny mistakes.
